headline: Nasdaq-100 futures recover part of Thursday's AI-led decline with volatility contained
body: Thursday's cash session closed the Nasdaq-100 down 1.39% at 30,725.81, in the lower third of a 30,556.40-31,125.13 range, after a Financial Times report that OpenAI told investors its annualized revenue was near $50 billion at the end of September rather than the roughly $70 billion previously reported. Oracle fell more than 5%, Nvidia close to 3%, AMD close to 4% and the Philadelphia semiconductor gauge 3.4%. Rising long-end yields and crude above $100 compounded the derating. Overnight, NQ December futures recovered to about 31,206-31,216, roughly 0.8% above a 30,969.50 settlement, holding the upper half of a 31,120-31,267 range after OpenAI pointed to annual revenue reaching or exceeding $70 billion by year-end. Crude has turned lower, with WTI near $90.56 and Brent near $102.82, and VIX near 15.3 sits below Thursday's 15.41 close. The recovery is therefore a two-way counter-move rather than observed one-way structure, which keeps Tail in the low band. Stress stays elevated on the unresolved AI-capex valuation question, a 10-year yield of 5.28% and a 30-year of 5.67% on the 7 October H.15 release, and an active Iran/Hormuz campaign in which a tanker was struck north of Qatar on 8 October. Shared Finviz context was unavailable for this run, so the assessment rests on independently verified sources.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 published hours are complete. Tail peaked at 28% (orange) in the 17:00Z hour on 8 October during the AI-led cash selloff, then decayed steadily through the U.S. close and the Asian and European sessions to 17% by the 10:00Z hour. Stress fell almost continuously from 72% at that peak to 46%, while Confidence held at 85-89% throughout. Dominant mode moved from trend-down at the selloff peak through mixed overnight to trend-up across the last four hours as futures recovered.
outlookSummary: The near-term path is dominated by two scheduled checkpoints and one structural boundary. The 13:30Z cash open and the 14:00Z Michigan preliminary release define a narrow window where gap continuation, if it appears, would be the first genuine Tail amplifier; Tail is lifted into the watch band for those hours on the mechanics of the events rather than on observed structure. Tail then decays through the midday and early-afternoon rotation hours before rising again for the power hour and the 20:00Z cash close, where Friday weekend de-risking can force a fast directional push. NQ futures close for the week at 21:00Z and do not reopen until Sunday 22:00Z, so the final fourteen forecast hours carry no tradeable price path: Tail and Stress fall because mean reversion cannot fail in a halted market, and Confidence decays with the age of the last live observation. Remaining weekend exposure is reopen-gap risk, principally from the unresolved AI-capex derating question, the 5.28% 10-year, and the active campaign against shipping outside the Strait of Hormuz.
